questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
I have always wanted to take environmental economics and they have a really good program for that at UiO. One of my professors in the course have previous taught at MIT and Harvard. This was his last semester at UiO (and I am really glad I had him) hence he has started at Stanford.
I also liked that it was close to home and I have alway wanted to explore the Norwegian nature.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was easy and I knew who to ask if I had any questions.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I didn't get any assistance. I knew where to pick up my keys and had the address for my house.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was easy. One can apply for housing at SiO and almost every exchange students will get housing.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I lived in a student village with almost 400 other students. We have a supermarket and bar in the village. There is a really good network between the students and people are nice. I thought it was a little far from the city center but the public transport is really good and it was quite close to campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I lived in a shared flat with five other exchange students.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I got all information at mail and knew who to ask if I had any questions.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I got help from the IT-support and the  studentinformation at my faculty.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got the courses I applied for.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: You can register for as many courses as you want and then shuffle between the classes before you deide with courses you would like to take. I didn't knew this and it would have been nice to now hence there were more courses I found interesting and this way one can figure it out after one have landed in the exchange life.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: It was similar to UCHP.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was the same as UCHP. 2 hoours of lecture every week and seminar every second week.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
ECON4820 – Strategic Competition
ECON4910 – Environmental Economics

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I would recommend them both. ECON4910 was really good hence we had one of the leading professors in that field but it was also a really hard course.
ECON4820 was really interesting and one the the best professors I have ever had. The course was well organized and the professor tried to make a perspective to the real world everytime we ended a topic.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I was sick a few times up here so expenses to got to the doctors. I spend around 2.000 DKK on doctors and medicine during my exchange.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: I expected alcohol to be expensive but meat is also expensive. Fish and tampons are really cheap.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There are a lot of associations at UiO one can join and people are open about one joining despite one is a exchange student.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Join the faculty café/bar and something where one live.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I went on a roundtrip to explore the Norwegian nature and I can really recommend that!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Yes it was. The culture is very similar to Denmark.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Just ask people, reach out and join things. Especially in the beginning.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Norwegians are "shy" but one you have contact with them they are so nice. So just dare to talk to them.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The nature and how outdoor people are. It's different from Denmark.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Apply for housing throgh SiO.
It is not as expensive as one think.
take part in the buddy week and be open minded when you arrive.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: That I got really good along with my flat mates. It is really important to feel good and at home where you live.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Getting started and feel at home in a new city. when you start from scratch. Find your way around, make your room cozy, find the nearest (and cheapest) supermarket and the energy to "be a part of everything" in the beginning.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: No

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
